headline: This 2013 law lets the Housing and Urban Development Department add or change rules for federally insured reverse mortgages to strengthen the program's finances.
what_it_does: It amends the National Housing Act, which governs federal mortgage insurance for reverse mortgages, also called home equity conversion mortgages. It lets the HUD Secretary set extra or different requirements through a notice or mortgagee letter when needed to improve the program's fiscal safety and soundness. Those requirements take effect as soon as HUD issues them.

who_it_affects.group: Elderly homeowners with federally insured reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: HUD can change the rules for their loans through notices or mortgagee letters, and those changes take effect when issued.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders and mortgage servicers that offer federally insured reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: They must follow any new or alternative HUD requirements issued under this authority as soon as they are published.

who_it_affects.group: Future borrowers considering a reverse mortgage
who_it_affects.how: Loan terms and eligibility rules may change over time as HUD uses this authority.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on August 9, 2013. Each new HUD requirement takes effect when HUD issues it.
